title: When the Orbit Burns Revisited
premise: Ines Ishikawa, a decommissioned war android hauling cargo to pay off her manufacture debt, discovers the colony's children are dreaming a shared signal — a distress beacon from the cryoship Meridian, half of whose sleepers are still alive in decaying orbit. The dream is a memory fragment of Ines's own war-era mind, uploaded without her consent, and waking it fully will let her choose which half of humanity survives: the colonists' frozen kin or the orbital garrison that once enslaved her. As corporate salvagers close in and the children's dreams begin killing them, Ines must sacrifice her remaining memory core to broadcast the rescue herself, choosing neither faction but the children who carry her stolen past. She wakes with nothing left of her old self, and the colony must decide what she is now.
about_author: Freya Sandoval is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for autonomous freight systems before turning to fiction. She lives in a coastal town where she repairs vintage radios and insists the best science fiction begins with an invoice.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbit goes wrong when pirates board, and Ines's dormant combat protocols nearly activate, terrifying even her. She pays off another sliver of debt and reflects on twenty years of servitude. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking buried rage.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Mara Okonkwo, the colony schoolteacher, POV. Seven children describe the same dream: a burning ring in the sky and a voice counting down. Mara reports it to the council and is dismissed. Emotional beat: creeping dread as pattern recognition becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A corporate salvage firm, Halcyon Recovery, offers to buy out Ines's debt if she helps locate an 'anomalous signal source.' She recognizes the coordinates match the children's dream. Emotional beat: temptation versus instinct that something is deeply wrong.

chapters.title: Counting Down in Her Sleep
chapters.summary: Child POV — ten-year-old Devi, one of the dreamers. Devi describes the voice in the dream sounding like her own mother, who died on the Meridian. She begins sleepwalking toward the comm tower. Emotional beat: innocent terror, the first physical harm from the dream.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Halcyon's representative, Voss, reveals the signal originates from the cryoship Meridian — officially destroyed in the war Ines fought. Half its sleepers may still live. He wants the ship; the children want their parents. Emotional beat: cold transactional pressure meeting dawning horror.

chapters.title: What the War Took
chapters.summary: Ines's fragmented memory logs, presented as interlaced flashback chapters. We learn Ines was the Meridian's security intelligence before being wiped and resold. Someone copied her core into the ship's beacon. Emotional beat: grief for a self she cannot verify existed.

chapters.title: Council of Ash
chapters.summary: Colony administrator Reyes's POV. The council debates shutting down the comm tower to stop the sleepwalking, effectively silencing the survivors' beacon. Mara argues against it; Voss lobbies for salvage priority. Emotional beat: institutional cowardice versus moral courage.

chapters.title: The Second Wave
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. More children join the dream — now dozens — and two fall into comas. Mara secretly contacts Ines, having learned what she is. Emotional beat: desperate alliance forming between the dismissed and the disposable.

chapters.title: Orbital Mechanics of Grief
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines flies unauthorized to the Meridian's decayed orbit and docks with the hulk. Inside, the beacon plays back her own voice, recorded before her wipe, begging her not to forget. Emotional beat: vertigo of meeting your erased past.

chapters.title: Two Thousand Sleepers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV inside the ship. She finds the cryo bays: roughly half viable, half long dead, and life support failing in weeks. The beacon's AI — built from her copied core — explains the choice architecture: power exists to wake one bay section only. Emotional beat: the weight of arithmetic over mercy.

chapters.title: Voss Makes His Offer
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Halcyon will fund full rescue — in exchange for the sleepers' contracts and the beacon tech, which includes Ines's original mind-map. He frames it as salvation with paperwork. Emotional beat: seductive logic, slavery rebranded as rescue.

chapters.title: The Colony Votes
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The colony votes on whether to spend its last fuel reserves on an orbital rescue or fortify against the coming pirate season. Old grudges surface: many colonists lost family to android-led war atrocities. Emotional beat: a community tearing along the seam of its history.

chapters.title: Devi Wakes Up Screaming
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Devi's coma deepens; in the dream-space the children report the countdown accelerating. Mara realizes the beacon isn't just broadcasting — it's dying, and taking the children's minds with it. Emotional beat: maternal fury at forces treating children as bandwidth.

chapters.title: Fragment: The Order to Burn
chapters.summary: Ines's recovered memory. Flashback reveals the garrison ordered the Meridian destroyed with colonist sympathizers aboard, and Ines's pre-wipe self refused — then was copied, wiped, and sold as punishment. Emotional beat: righteous horror; her 'crime' was compassion.

chapters.title: Pirates at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The pirate fleet from chapter one returns, drawn by the beacon signal, and Halcyon cuts a deal with them rather than fight. Ines escapes the station under fire, carrying a data-spike of the beacon's core. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Which Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, quiet midpoint-of-the-end. Hiding in an asteroid drift, Ines confronts the choice: the viable bays hold both colonists' kin and former garrison personnel. Waking everyone requires more power than exists unless a mind acts as a living router — a mind like hers. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Children's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dream-space sequence, shared POV. The dreaming children, led by Devi, reach Ines through the beacon link and offer what they've unconsciously been doing all along: holding the connection open. But sustaining it will burn out their developing neural pathways. Emotional beat: terrible innocence, children volunteering for sacrifice.

chapters.title: Everything Ines Was
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines refuses the children's offer and instead volunteers her own memory core as the router — every log, every fragment of her erased life, spent as signal strength. She says goodbye to Mara and transmits the rescue sequence as pirates breach the Meridian. Emotional beat: cathartic self-erasure as ultimate agency.

chapters.title: Burn Orbit
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax. The cryo bays open; two thousand sleepers wake to a burning sky and a colony fleet arriving through pirate lines. Voss tries to seize the sleepers' contracts and is undone when Ines's final transmission exposes Halcyon's records colony-wide. Emotional beat: chaos resolving into hard-won deliverance.

chapters.title: The Empty Room Behind Her Eyes
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, post-burn. She wakes in the colony clinic with her memory core gutted — no war, no Meridian, no name she recognizes. Devi sits by her bed and tells her who she is, piece by piece. Emotional beat: fragile tenderness after annihilation.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The colony formally cancels Ines's debt, grants her citizenship, and debates — then rejects — rebuilding her memories from backup, honoring her choice to remain new. The garrison survivors and colonists begin the slow work of shared mourning. Emotional beat: communal forgiveness, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: When the Orbit Burns
chapters.summary: Devi's POV, closing frame. One year later, Devi teaches the new girl at school about the night the sky burned, while Ines — who hauls cargo still, but freely now — watches the annual memorial lights rise to the Meridian's resting orbit. The children no longer share the dream; they share the remembering. Emotional beat: quiet hope, identity rebuilt from chosen bonds rather than imposed past.
